text:
amanda: Heads up — seeing 3 nodes in gpu-pool-us-west2 go NotReady and kube shows pods stuck Pending/NoSchedule for all GPU workloads. Lifting to #eng-infra since this affects Dedicated capacity.
amanda: infra alert -> infra-bot:GPU_ALERT: node/gpu-ustw-04 NotReady (device-plugin failed)
infra-bot: [ALERT] GPU capacity degradation: 3 nodes NotReady in gpu-pool-us-west2. Incident created: INC-20260315-32
zack: copy. can you paste the device-plugin logs from one of the nodes?
amanda: pasted logs from gpu-ustw-04:
```
I0315 12:07:11.123456 1 plugin.go:230] Starting NVIDIA device plugin
E0315 12:07:12.004321 1 plugin.go:312] failed to list devices: nvidia-container-cli: initialization error: driver error: cannot open /dev/nvidiactl: No such file or directory
Error: failed to start plugin: failed to initialize NVML: Unknown
``` 
priya: that looks like driver not loaded on the host. any recent node image rollouts? tom: yes, node pool had a staged kernel+image update at 02:00 UTC this morning.
amanda: node pool event: "rolling-update image v2026-03-kernel5.18 -> v2026-03-kernel5.19" — happened ~02:10.
zack: likely kernel upgrade without rebuilding nvidia modules -> nvidia modules missing -> /dev/nvidia* absent -> device-plugin crashes -> nodes NotReady
sre-oncall: confirm: kubelet status shows NodeStatus: NotReady (KubeletNotReady) and condition: RuntimeUnhealthy on these nodes.
priya: quick mitigation options: 1) cordon+drain and let autoscaler replace nodes (if image is bad) 2) attempt to reinstall driver modules on the node set 3) roll back node image to previous version
tom: autoscaler note: cluster-autoscaler won't terminate nodes in use; but if we cordon+drain and pods are scheduleable elsewhere, CA should scale down old nodes. we should be careful about GPU job queuing causing scaling churn.
amanda: tried `kubectl cordon gpu-ustw-04` and `kubectl drain` — drain hangs because device-plugin DaemonSet has pod(s) with pod disruption budget? also some infra DaemonSets pinned.
zack: add --ignore-daemonsets during drain; but if driver isn't present, kubelet won't report GPU allocatable and draining GPU jobs fails.
priya: can we restart the nvidia-driver DaemonSet first? it won't help if /dev device nodes are missing on the host (module not loaded).
tom: check `dmesg` for module load errors — amanda, can you paste kernel errors?
amanda: dmesg excerpt:
```
[    5.234567] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel.
[    5.234578] nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol module_layout
[    5.234589] nvidia: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing - tainting kernel
[    5.235000] nvidia: Unknown symbol nvidia_p2p_map (err -2)
```
zack: yep — module ABI mismatch due to kernel rev. modules didn't build for new kernel.
priya: immediate plan? rollback node image to previous kernel (fastest but disruptive), or trigger an in-place rebuild of kernel modules (requires DKMS or packaged driver matching kernel). which approach is faster?
amanda: rollback would reprovision nodes from older image; takes ~10-15m per node but CA will take time to reschedule.
tom: alternative: create a short-lived Job that runs on affected nodes with privileged host mount and installs packaged NVIDIA drivers that match current kernel (we have driver packages in s3). risk: installation might fail if kernel headers missing.
sre-oncall: we need to preserve customer SLA. suggest: 1) cordon affected nodes 2) spin up extra warm GPU nodes in a temporary spare node pool with compatible image in us-west2 3) migrate critical jobs 4) rollback image for problem pool afterwards.
zack: agree. also add a short-term autoscaler override: bump desired count of warm-pool by +3 to ensure capacity.
priya: cost note: spinning spare nodes will increase cost by ~3x for the hour; but avoids customer impact. prepared a rough estimate in chat.
amanda: starting actions now: cordon affected nodes, create warm-pool-us-west2 (image v2026-02-kernel5.18), scale to +3.
amanda: `kubectl cordon gpu-ustw-04 gpu-ustw-05 gpu-ustw-06` — done.
amanda: provisioning warm nodes — request sent to infra API: create nodepool warm-gpu-usw2 image=v2026-02 count=3
infra-bot: [TASK] nodepool/warm-gpu-usw2: creation request accepted. request id np-req-778
zack: while warm pool coming up, can we try a non-destructive workaround: mount old kernel modules from image snapshot and create device nodes manually? risky.
priya: don't do manual dev nodes on prod unless we're out of options.
tom: ops checklist for rollback path: 1) cordon + drain affected nodes 2) set nodepool image to previous 3) trigger rolling replace 4) monitor device-plugin logs and node allocatable GPU
amanda: warm pool is healthy, pods are drifting over. critical CI GPU jobs moved.
amanda: infra-bot reports new nodes registered: gpu-warm-01..03
sre-oncall: observing reduced Pending counts. GPU pods scheduled to new nodes.
zack: we should also push a quick change to upgrade playbooks: required preflight for node-image rollouts: verify nvidia module builds for target kernel, and run driver smoke test (nvidia-smi) via a preflight DaemonSet.
priya: agree. create an actionable ticket: "node image rollout: ensure nvidia kernel module ABI compatibility + preflight checks". priya->assign infra team.
priya: assigned ticket INFRA-1427.
amanda: once load stabilizes, we'll mark incident closed and schedule formal postmortem.
infra-bot: [INCIDENT] INC-20260315-32 updated: mitigation in place, partial recovery. status: monitoring.
zack: longer-term: add node pool label to prevent simultaneous kernel/image upgrade on >20% of GPU capacity, and add canary nodes to test image before full rollout.
priya: add to INFRA-1427: "canary size, preflight smoke, rollback automation, and autoscaler integration tests".
tom: final note: make sure Dedicated customers using reserved capacity are notified — emailing CS to flag impacted customers.
amanda: emailing CS and ops now. closing loop once all GPU nodes report Ready.
amanda: last check: nodes gpu-ustw-04..06 are still NotReady; new warm nodes are serving traffic. monitoring for 30m and then decide about rollback vs rebuild.
zack: 👍
